summary: In the break room, Glorp and Kreeb turn the post-corridor disclosure procedure into two competing ideas of care while Jax becomes their reluctant test case. The comedy comes from Glorp needing proof that the procedure is voluntary, Kreeb insisting that it actually be voluntary, and Jax discovering that a genuine exit is harder to resent than a trap.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Break room immediately after the corridor release. Microwave remains taped off. Glorp and Kreeb arrange a small semicircle of folding chairs. One chair is labeled FEELINGS DISCLOSURE SEAT A; the taped-to-itself drone remains nearby as WITNESS DRONE. Jax enters only because he was trying to get lunch.

Panel 2 — Glorp and Kreeb both look toward Jax. Jax recognizes the shape of the trap before either of them asks for anything. Kreeb stays calm and genuinely non-coercive; Glorp is already clutching the form.

Panel 3 — Jax sits in FEELINGS DISCLOSURE SEAT A but angles the chair toward the exit and plants one foot for a quick departure. Kreeb notices without correcting him. Glorp notices and wants to document it.

Panel 4 — Glorp hands Jax the lunch-adjacent form. Jax studies it like hostile paperwork. Kreeb watches the interaction, increasingly aware that Glorp is treating proof of voluntariness as more important than voluntariness itself.

Panel 5 — Glorp and Kreeb finally disagree directly about what the procedure is for. Jax sits between them, unexpectedly interested because the disagreement is now about whether people are allowed to leave.

Panel 6 — Kreeb explicitly gives Jax an unqualified exit. Jax half-rises, then pauses because the absence of coercion removes his favorite thing to push against. Glorp, alarmed by the new ambiguity, reaches for another tab.

summary: Jax, Mira and Zib privately review the stabilizer footage. Mira finds the useful pattern, Zib establishes that Jax did not cause the mechanical fault, and both of them refuse to let that fact erase his choice to avoid reporting it. The trio turns a technical evidence review into a precise, funny distinction between causing a problem and preserving one.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — At a small break-room wall screen, Mira scrubs hallway footage while Zib stands with a practical tool and Jax leans beside them. The room is quieter now; this is a three-person postmortem, not a staff meeting.

Panel 2 — Footage freezes on Jax opening the stabilizer panel and slowly closing it halfway. Mira leans in close to the screen, delighted by the mechanical/crystal rhythm despite herself. Jax watches his own bad decision happen in silence.
Panel 3 — Zib inspects the image and his tool, then gives Jax the narrow good news: the gate was already sticking. Jax brightens too quickly.
Panel 4 — Zib immediately takes the victory back: Jax saw the fault and tried to disappear into the room. Mira is amused because the technical exoneration and interpersonal indictment are both true.
Panel 5 — Mira summarizes the situation with scientific precision that accidentally sounds like praise. Jax accepts the compliment before Zib can stop him.
Panel 6 — Zib makes the future expectation concrete: call before the problem develops a social life. Jax tests the boundary with one last joke; Mira is already tempted to write the phrase down.

summary: Astra, Mira and Pixa process StarTrust's automated classification of the stardust as useful waste. Mira is delighted by the scientific absurdity, Pixa quantifies the value without social tact, and Astra discovers the exact corporate outcome she wants: enough usefulness to keep the branch alive, not enough importance to attract serious attention. Their relief turns immediately into alarm when the system offers a yield-optimization consult.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — A small admin-hub monitor flashes UNUSUAL MATERIAL FLAG — CLASSIFY USEFUL WASTE. Only Astra, Mira and Pixa are at the station console. Astra goes pale; Mira lights up.

Panel 2 — Pixa opens a clean corporate estimate. Astra asks the only question she cares about: how useful. Pixa reports positive salvage/novelty value and the operating-status implication with cheerful precision.

Panel 3 — Pixa clarifies that the branch is still not strategically interesting. Astra visibly relaxes for the first time. Mira realizes that 'useful but unimportant' is Astra's ideal corporate status.

Panel 4 — Mira studies a small residue sample and states the real pattern carefully: cleaner growth followed people stopping the obvious concealment. Astra immediately blocks any attempt to turn that correlation into an emotional production target; Pixa records the distinction.
Panel 5 — Astra and Mira share a brief, aligned look: science can describe the byproduct, management can protect the people, and neither wants StarTrust to confuse the two.
Panel 6 — Monitor adds WOULD YOU LIKE TO SCHEDULE A YIELD OPTIMIZATION CONSULT? All three stare at it. The scene ends on the shared recognition that corporate has already found the wrong lesson.

summary: The crew refuses to let useful stardust become emotional extraction. In one small group, Astra discovers that Glorp's bureaucracy can protect people while Kreeb draws a hard line between invitation and coercion. In a second trio, Noola gives Jax permission to refuse without performing, while Brick turns a harmless MAYBE LATER card into noir intimidation. The page makes consent and boundaries funny without turning them into a lecture.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Break-room side table. Glorp arrives with binder tab USEFUL WASTE / FEELINGS / LUNCH; Kreeb carries simple circle cards. Astra meets them without the rest of the crew. Glorp is already trying to prevent corporate metrics from swallowing the social process.

Panel 2 — Astra assumes she must stop another procedure from becoming emotional optimization. Glorp surprises her: the document in hand is a prohibition, not a program. Kreeb calmly backs the boundary.

Panel 3 — Astra realizes Glorp's anticipatory bureaucracy is useful here. Kreeb defines the circle as voluntary community practice, not a production input. The three reach actual alignment without a meeting multiplying around them.

Panel 4 — Elsewhere in the break room, Jax delivers his carefully rehearsed anti-emotion-mining position to Noola. Brick occupies a nearby patch of shadow, saying nothing. Noola immediately identifies the rehearsal.
Panel 5 — Noola tells Jax he can simply say no without turning refusal into a performance. Jax is genuinely disarmed by the efficiency. Brick silently picks up a card labeled MAYBE LATER.

Panel 6 — Brick turns MAYBE LATER so it faces Jax like evidence. Jax feels absurdly threatened by stationery. Noola reminds him the answer is still his; Jax admits that real permission makes the whole thing harder to dodge.
